title: Wren and the Archive
premise: Oscar Sandoval, an insurance investigator sent to assess the failing colony of Meridian's Rest, discovers the settlement was deliberately written off by the corporation that founded it—left to die quietly so its debts could be erased. The colony's children have begun sharing a single dream: a voice calling from a relay station at the edge of dead space, an inheritance left by the colony's first engineer. As Oscar records the truth for a claim no one will pay, he and the children realize the dream is a distress signal counting down to the relay's final shutdown—and that the corporation has sent a crew to erase all evidence, including witnesses. Racing across the dying colony, they reach the relay and broadcast the archive of everything the company buried, ending with Meridian's Rest saved not by rescue but by exposure, and Oscar choosing to stay as the children's reluctant guardian.
about_author: Jonah Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years documenting losses at sea before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burning science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people systems forget.

chapters.title: The Adjuster Arrives
chapters.summary: Oscar Sandoval lands on Meridian's Rest to close out a routine claim on a collapsing atmospheric processor. His POV establishes his methodical detachment and the colony's eerie quiet—fewer people than the manifests claim. Emotional beat: professional curiosity shading into unease as he notices children watching him from rooftops.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Missing
chapters.summary: Oscar audits the colony's records and finds systematic discrepancies: deaths logged as relocations, equipment failures logged as sabotage by ghosts. POV alternates between Oscar and Mara Voss, the colony's exhausted administrator who is hiding something. Emotional beat: the dawning sense that the paperwork itself is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Twelve-year-old Ila Reyes wakes screaming alongside every other child in the dormitory block—they dreamed the same corridor, the same humming door. Ila's POV introduces the dream's details: a relay, a countdown, a woman's voice saying 'remember us.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as adults dismiss them.

chapters.title: The First Engineer
chapters.summary: Mara reluctantly shows Oscar sealed archives about Dr. Yuen Sefa, the colony's founding engineer who died decades ago but whose maintenance logs continue updating. Oscar's POV; he recognizes posthumous automation—or a deliberate inheritance. Emotional beat: awe at Sefa's foresight, dread at what she anticipated.

chapters.title: Claim Denied
chapters.summary: Oscar transmits his preliminary findings to his employer and receives an immediate order to cease investigation and return. His POV reveals corporate pressure he's felt before on other forgotten colonies. Emotional beat: the quiet humiliation of a man whose job is to make losses official rather than real.

chapters.title: What the Dream Wants
chapters.summary: Ila and the older children map their shared dream against the colony's actual layout and find it matches a buried conduit running toward the edge of dead space. Ila's POV. Emotional beat: the thrill of a secret that belongs entirely to them, and the first argument about whether to tell the adults.

chapters.title: A Man Who Counts Losses
chapters.summary: Oscar interviews the colony's oldest resident, who remembers Sefa warning that the corporation would one day need Meridian's Rest to disappear. Oscar's POV deepens his crisis of professional identity. Emotional beat: grief for every claim he closed without looking underneath.

chapters.title: The Company Ship
chapters.summary: A corporate vessel enters orbit unannounced—officially a 'welfare inspection,' carrying security personnel and a data-wipe team. Oscar's POV, recognizing the ship class from prior erasure operations. Emotional beat: cold terror; the timeline just collapsed.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: The inspectors seal communications and begin 'relocating' colonists to the orbital transfer station. Mara's POV as she realizes relocation means disappearance, and she chooses to help the children instead of complying. Emotional beat: an ordinary administrator becoming, unwillingly, a resistor.

chapters.title: The Conduit
chapters.summary: Ila leads six children into the buried conduit guided by the dream, while Oscar covers their escape by falsifying his own reports. Split POV between Ila underground and Oscar above. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing—strangers now conspirators.

chapters.title: Sefa's Voice
chapters.summary: Deep in the conduit, the children reach a waystation where Sefa's recorded messages explain the truth: the relay holds the full corporate archive, and the dream is her failsafe, keyed to young minds the company never monitored. Ila's POV. Emotional beat: inheriting a mission from a dead woman who trusted them.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Oscar is detained by the inspection team's lead, Auditor Kessler, who offers him reinstatement if he produces the children. Oscar's POV in a tense cat-and-mouse conversation. Emotional beat: temptation offered and refused—the moment he stops being an instrument.

chapters.title: Dead Space Crossing
chapters.summary: The children's stolen crawler crosses the radiation belt toward the relay while the dream grows louder and more urgent—a countdown now measured in days. Ila's POV, lyrical and frightened. Emotional beat: childhood ending deliberately, chosen.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Mara and remaining adults stage a diversion at the spaceport, buying the crawler time at the cost of their own capture. Mara's POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics—bureaucratic sabotage, quiet courage.

chapters.title: Relay
chapters.summary: The children reach the relay station and meet its caretaker: a decaying android carrying Sefa's final personality imprint, who has been maintaining the beacon alone for thirty years. Ila's POV. Emotional beat: meeting the dreamer; grief and welcome in the same breath.

chapters.title: Kessler Descends
chapters.summary: Kessler's strike team tracks the crawler and assaults the relay's surface approach. Oscar, escaped custody, arrives ahead of them through the old mining tunnels. Oscar's POV. Emotional beat: redemption through arrival—he chose this side in time.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: In the relay core, the children and Sefa's imprint begin uploading the archive—debt cancellations, engineered famines, forty erased colonies—to every open channel in inhabited space. Ila's POV interwoven with the archive's terrible contents. Emotional beat: the power of testimony against the power of silence.

chapters.title: Signal Jammed
chapters.summary: Kessler seizes the transmitter array mid-upload; the broadcast stalls at sixty percent. Oscar confronts Kessler physically and morally, offering himself in exchange for the transmission window. Oscar's POV. Emotional beat: climax of will—an accountant of losses spending himself as the final asset.

chapters.title: One Hundred Percent
chapters.summary: Ila completes the upload using the dream-link itself, synchronizing every child on the colony and in the transfer station to hold the signal open. The archive goes out; Kessler's authority evaporates as his own superiors go silent. Ila's POV. Emotional beat: triumph that feels like exhaustion, not victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Response ships arrive—not the company's, but independent settlements answering the broadcast. Kessler is taken into custody by his own escort. Oscar's POV, watching the sky fill with unfamiliar generosity. Emotional beat: disbelief softening into hope.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: The colonists debate their future: return to the revived company, join the independents, or hold Meridian's Rest themselves under Sefa's charter, which named the children as heirs. Mara's POV. Emotional beat: a community deciding it deserves to exist.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Months later, Oscar has stayed, teaching the children investigation as a form of care; Ila names the rebuilt relay 'Wren' after the smallest bird that sings anyway. Final shared dream: Sefa's voice, at peace, going quiet. Alternating POVs closing on Ila and Oscar together. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance accepted, home declared.
